alignments.note: Finite הָיָה carries the clause's person and number and takes the subject pronoun (rule 17).
Second periphrastic הָיָה; the ASV writes no separate word for it (rule 22).
Article takes the *the* before its own word (rule 29).
Rectum takes the *of*, discontinuous around the article.
Finite verb recast as an English passive with its auxiliaries and phrasal particle.
Object suffix promoted to the subject of the English passive; it keeps the pronoun written for it (rule 18).

Preposition. The ASV writes a word for each morpheme of מִשָּׁם, so rule 2 splits the pair, exactly as it does for the same two morphemes at 2KI.17.27; dropping *among* leaves this preposition holding the *from* it is rendered by throughout the chapter, which is the subtraction test rule 30 prescribes.

Resumptive locative adverb; *among* is what the ASV spends on it in the recast relative phrase *from among whom*, as *thence* is at 2KI.17.27. The competing reading, taken by the verse pass, fused מִן and שָׁם as *from among* under rule 30 and headed it on the preposition.

review_notes: The chapter analysed מִן plus a resumptive שָׁם two ways: split at 2KI.17.27 (*from* / *thence*) and fused at 2KI.17.33 (*from among*). Rule 30 lets a differing ASV rendering license a differing analysis, as it does for מִפְּנֵי at 17.8 and 17.11, so the two verses are reconciled by testing 17.33 on its own terms rather than by imposing 17.27.

On those terms the fusion does not hold. Rule 30's condition is that no morpheme owns a part of the shared rendering, and *from* is the word this chapter spends on מִן in eleven other units, so the subtraction test finds that morpheme's rendering intact when *among* is dropped. The reading was unstable in either direction besides: a fusion whose one rendering does not carry שָׁם's sense is what rule 30 forbids outright, and a fusion whose rendering does carry it hands שָׁם a word of its own.

*among* is placed as what the ASV spends on the resumptive locative in *from among whom*, on the reasoning rule 32 uses for a directive he and rule 40 for a preposition, namely whether the ASV spends an English word on what that morpheme contributes. אֲשֶׁר keeps its own *whom* and no morpheme is left holding two English words.
